correctness.rationale: The primary paper proves B=0π(T) with T Tribonacci φ fixed point and π(0)=100, π(1)=101, π(2)=10. Recomputed all three φ³-image blocks of lengths 20,17,11 and all five actual adjacent Tribonacci pairs 00,01,02,10,20. Length≤11 factors lie in six explicit finite cover words, since spanning two boundaries would require ≥13 letters. Independent enumeration recovers distinct palindrome counts at lengths 1..11: 2,2,2,2,2,1,2,1,1,0,0. Nonexistence at lengths 10 and 11 excludes all larger palindromes by their centers. Total 15, longest unique 100101001 at length 9; prefix 24 has 14 and prefix 25 all 15, hence sharp defect N-15 for N≥25. Finite cover proves infinite statement, rather than 100,000-letter sampling.

evidence: The word is not reversal-closed: 1011 occurs but 1101 does not; it is not complement-symmetric since 0010 occurs and 1101 does not.
General reversal-closed/complement-symmetric word theorems do not directly apply.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader palindromic complexity theorems with symmetry hypotheses cannot imply the spectrum for this specific non-symmetric word.

value.rationale: This is a complete and sharp palindromic-language classification of a specifically studied nonuniform morphic word, with exact finite spectrum, unique longest palindrome and first saturation threshold. Such complete factor-language invariants are natural in combinatorics on words and are not a routine calculation from factor complexity.

limitations: Specific contiguous factors of Kimberling word B, not all Rote or morphic words.
Finite 100000-symbol check is supplementary only; the infinite claim is established via the six-word cover.
